title: How to Set Up an AI Storefront for Your Link in Bio

blocks.text: Most “set up your link in bio” guides end with a stack of buttons. That is a classic link page: list URLs, hope people pick the right one, answer the rest in DMs.

An AI storefront is different. Followers tap one link, talk to an assistant grounded in your knowledge, open your offers, or start a Work with me request — without bouncing through three other apps. That is what PingMyBio is built for.

Short answer: Sign up → claim pingmybio.com/you → fill Profile → add Knowledge and FAQs → publish offers (and Work with me if brands matter) → paste the URL in Instagram/TikTok. Skip the theme rabbit hole; spend the time on answers the assistant can use.
Classic link page vs AI storefront
What you need before you start
An email you check (login + Inbox alerts)
A short bio and a clear photo or brand mark
At least one offer you actually sell (a linked offer, freebie, or Work with me)
The answers you already repeat in DMs (“how much?”, “what’s included?”, “do you work with brands?”)
Step 1 — Create your page and claim the URL
Go to Create a page.
Sign up and complete setup for your creator profile.
Claim a short slug. Your public page will be pingmybio.com/yourname.
Use the handle people already know from Instagram or TikTok when you can. Changing it later means updating every bio that links to you.
Early access note: first 100 creators get five months free on the current offer — confirm on the signup screen.
Step 2 — Finish Profile (this is the storefront header)
Open App → Profile. This is what fans see before they chat.
Display name and handle
Short positioning line (who you help + outcome)
Photo / brand image
Social links you want next to the hub (optional)
Keep the headline job-shaped: “Career coach for mid-level PMs” beats “Creator | Speaker | Vibes.”
Step 3 — Teach the assistant with Knowledge + FAQs
Open App → Knowledge. This is the difference between an AI storefront and a button page.
Add:
Topics — how you work, who you serve, what you do not take
FAQs — the exact Q&A you paste into DMs today
Write the way you talk. Short answers beat essays. Include prices or ranges if you are comfortable publishing them; otherwise say how pricing works and what to ask for.

Also add offer-level knowledge when you create each product (private notes the assistant uses when someone asks about that specific session or download). Fans never need to see the raw notes — they feel the answers.
Without Knowledge, the assistant has nothing solid to say. With it, “how much / what’s included / can we collab?” stops living only in your phone.
Step 4 — Add offers that match what you sell
Open App → Offers → add an offer:
Linked offer — title, description, and a URL to where fans buy, book, or watch
Freebie — something fans unlock with email
Work with me — brands send collab requests (set rates and rules in Studio)
For each linked offer:
Clear title and destination URL
What’s included in plain language
Assistant notes / FAQs for this offer when you have them
Publish when the link is ready
One sharp offer beats eight vague buttons. You can add more after the first path works.
Step 5 — Test the page like a fan
Open pingmybio.com/yourname in a private window
Ask the assistant a real question from your DMs
Tap an offer and confirm the link goes where you expect
If Work with me is live, send a test collab and confirm it lands in Inbox
Step 6 — Go live on Instagram or TikTok
You only get one bio URL on each app. Paste your PingMyBio link.
Instagram: Edit profile → Website (or links) → save → tap it as a viewer.
TikTok: Use the phone app → Edit profile → Website field. If the field is missing, see our TikTok link in bio guide (follower / business-account rules change by region).
In captions, say what happens after the tap: “Ask the bio which session fits” beats “link in bio” alone.
Launch checklist
[ ] Slug is the handle you want long-term
[ ] Profile photo + one-line positioning
[ ] At least five real FAQs or topic notes in Knowledge
[ ] One live offer with a clear next step (link or freebie)
[ ] Assistant answers a DM-style question correctly in a private window
[ ] Instagram and/or TikTok Website field points at your page
[ ] You know where Inbox shows fan chats and collab requests
Common mistakes
Empty Knowledge — the page looks smart; the answers are not
Ten half-finished offers — fans stall; ship one path
Pricing only in your head — the assistant cannot invent a rate card you never wrote
Linking Instagram to Instagram — waste the one URL slot
Treating it like Linktree — if you only need a list, compare tools and pick a list product
FAQ
How long does setup take? A usable page can go live the same day: profile, a handful of FAQs, and one offer. Polish Knowledge as questions come in.
Do I need Classic mode? No. PingMyBio is an AI bio. Classic link lists are what other tools do. Use those if you only want buttons.
Can I use this for Instagram and TikTok? Yes — same URL in both Website fields. One hub, two apps.
Is PingMyBio free to try? Check the signup screen for the current early-access offer (including the first-100 creators promo when it is still open).

Google’s first result for Linktree alternative is still a Reddit thread: “Best link in bio tool / Linktree alternative?” That is the real brief. Creators are not shopping for a prettier button page. They are trying to stop losing DMs, bookings, and brand asks after someone taps the bio.

This roundup matches that intent. PingMyBio is our product — an intelligent bio hub, not a Linktree clone. The other tools below are the ones that actually show up next to that query (Solo, roundup blogs, Lnk.Bio, Hostinger-style lists). Verify current pricing on each vendor before you pay.
Short answer: Keep Linktree if you only need a list. Switch if your bio has to answer, book, or sell without sending people through three other apps.
Why people look for a Linktree alternative
Linktree won because it is fast and familiar. The complaint in 2026 is the same one on that Instagram Marketing thread: the page is a parking lot.
Followers still DM “how much / what’s included / can we collab?”
Selling and booking usually hop out to Gumroad, Calendly, Stan, or a form
Lower paid tiers still take a cut of digital sales (Linktree has published 12% on Free and 9% on mid plans; 0% is the expensive tier — confirm live)
A list cannot recommend the right offer at 1am
If your Instagram or TikTok bio is just YouTube + newsletter, stay. If the bio is how you get clients, you need a different job from the URL.
How to pick (ignore the 20-tool listicles)
Most ranking articles dump 11–20 logos. Use the job instead:
Pretty links, lowest effort — Linktree, Lnk.Bio, Carrd
Personal brand one-pager — Solo
Media kit and brand deals — Beacons
Fast digital checkout — Stan
Bio that answers, routes offers, and takes collabs — PingMyBio
Best Linktree alternatives at a glance
PingMyBio — Intelligent bio: assistant + offers + Work with me. Create a page.
Solo — Designed “best Linktree alternative” landing page; personal site / link hub.
Beacons — Creator suite (store, email, media kit). Watch fees on the free plan.
Stan Store — Mobile checkout for products and sessions. Paid from day one.
Lnk.Bio — Cheap / lifetime link page. Fine for lists, thin for a real business.
Carrd — Custom one-pager. You embed everyone else’s checkout and calendar.
1. PingMyBio — best when the bio should answer and convert
What it is: A PingMyBio page at pingmybio.com/you. Followers tap one link and can talk to an assistant trained on your knowledge, open your offers, or start a Work with me collab request.
That is the opposite of Linktree’s job. Linktree lists destinations. PingMyBio is the destination: profile + conversation, then the offer.
Use it if: You sell services or expertise (coaching, workshops, brand collabs) and you are tired of repeating yourself in DMs.
Skip it if: You only want a grid of buttons, Shopify merch, or a theme picker. We are not trying to be a prettier Linktree.
2. Solo — best “I just want a nicer hub”
Solo’s own page targets this exact keyword. It is a personal site / link hub with more design control than a raw list. Good when the problem is branding, not inbound questions.
Skip it if: People tap your bio and still need a human or an assistant to pick an offer.
3. Beacons — best all-in-one creator dashboard

Beacons shows up in almost every alternative roundup because the free plan is wide: links, store, email, media kit. The tradeoff is fees on lower tiers and a page that still does not run the “which session is right for me?” conversation.
Use it if: Brand deals and a self-updating media kit are the product.
4. Stan Store — best checkout, still a storefront

Stan is what people mean when they say “Linktree but I actually get paid.” One-tap digital checkout, bookings, courses. No free plan worth planning around. Your page is still a menu, not a conversation.
Use it if: You already know they came to buy a download or a call and you want the shortest cart.
5. Lnk.Bio — best budget list

Google’s AI Overview for this query cites Lnk.Bio for a reason: it is the cheap/lifetime answer in almost every “free Linktree alternative” article. Lists links. Optional shop on paid. Not a client machine.
6. Carrd — best if you want to design it yourself

Carrd is a landing-page builder, not a creator OS. Gorgeous one-pagers for ~$19/year. You wire Stripe, Calendly, and forms yourself. Fine for a portfolio. Painful if you wanted the bio to handle questions.
Free Linktree alternatives (what that Reddit thread actually asks)
“Free” in this category usually means free list, not free business.
Linktree Free — unlimited links; selling is where the cut hits
Lnk.Bio / Carrd free tiers — page exists; commerce is bolted on
Beacons Free — lots of features; sales fees
PingMyBio — create a page; first 100 creators get five months free on the current offer (confirm on the signup screen)
If the only requirement is “no monthly bill for a button list,” Lnk.Bio or Carrd win. If the requirement is “stop living in DMs,” free lists do not solve it.
Linktree vs PingMyBio
Linktree: many links, huge integrations, everyone recognizes the page
PingMyBio: one hub — assistant, offers, and Work with me next to the conversation
Same Instagram bio slot. Different product. PingMyBio’s wedge is talk first, then the right next step.
FAQ

What is the best Linktree alternative in 2026? There is no single winner. For a simple list, Linktree or Lnk.Bio. For checkout, Stan. For brand kits, Beacons. For a bio that answers and books services, PingMyBio.

Is there a free Linktree alternative? Yes — Linktree’s free plan, Lnk.Bio, Carrd, and Beacons all have free entry points. Free usually still means a list of links or a fee on sales. Check each site before you switch.

What is the best Linktree alternative for Instagram or TikTok? Any of the above can sit in the bio. Instagram and TikTok only give you one URL. Pick the tool that matches what happens after the tap: list, store, or conversation.

What is the best Linktree alternative for coaches? Coaches need answers, a booking path, and a way to capture leads — not twelve buttons. PingMyBio is built for that. Pensight-style tools still win if live video classroom is the whole product.

Will switching from Linktree hurt my traffic? You change one URL in Instagram/TikTok. Old Linktree links keep working until you unpublish them. The ranking risk is Google, not the social bio: this page is how people find an alternative; your handle is how fans arrive.

title: TikTok Link in Bio — How to Add It (and What to Put There)

blocks.text: Google’s first result for TikTok link in bio is a Reddit thread: “Can't add a link in my TikTok bio.” The rest of the page is TikTok’s own help doc, Shopify/Bitly/Later how-tos, and YouTube walkthroughs. That is the query: how do I get a clickable URL, then what should it be.

Short answer: Add the URL in Edit profile → Website on the phone app. If the field is missing, you are usually on a personal account under TikTok’s follower/business rules. Put a hub there, not your Instagram. TikTok only gives you one link.
What “link in bio” means on TikTok

On TikTok, link in bio means: look at the creator’s profile. There is (or should be) a website under the bio text. Captions say “link in bio” because videos cannot carry a normal outbound link the way a YouTube description can.
It is not a special TikTok product. It is that one website field plus whatever page you pointed at.
How to add a TikTok link in bio
Do this on the TikTok mobile app. Desktop usually cannot set the clickable Website field.
Open your profile (you icon).
Tap Edit profile.
Find Website (not only Bio).
Paste a full URL, including https://.
Save. Open your profile as a viewer and tap it.
If Website is missing, skip to the troubleshooting section. Do not paste a long URL into Bio and expect it to be tappable — description text is not the Website field.
Official path for connecting accounts/sites: TikTok Support — link a website or social media account.
Can’t add a link in your TikTok bio
That Reddit thread is still #1 because this keeps happening. Typical causes:

Personal account, not enough followers. TikTok has long gated the Website field (often around 1,000 followers for personal accounts). Thresholds and countries change — believe the app, not a blog from last year.

Still a personal account. Switch: profile → menu → Settings and privacy → Account → Switch to Business Account, then try Edit profile again. Some regions also ask for business registration if you are under the follower bar.
You are on desktop. Use the phone app.
App is stale. Update TikTok and retry.
Region. Some markets get the field later. If Support says it should be there and it is not, it is a TikTok account issue, not your landing page.

Workaround if Website will not appear: put a short, typeable URL in the Bio text (not clickable). Use something people can remember, like pingmybio.com/you. Ugly. Better than nothing until the field unlocks.
What to put in the TikTok link in bio
You get one URL. Wasting it on a raw Instagram, a five-page Linktree, or a homepage with no next step is how views die in DMs.
Put a page that can:
Answer “how much / what’s included / can we collab?”
Route them to the right offer or a Work with me request
Keep the next step on one URL
That is what PingMyBio is for: pingmybio.com/yourname — assistant from your knowledge, offers, and collab path on the same page.
A Linktree-style list is fine if you only need buttons. If TikTok traffic asks questions, a list sends them back to comments. See Linktree alternatives if you are choosing tools.
Say it in the video. “Link in bio” in the caption plus a spoken “book from my bio” beats a silent URL.
TikTok Shop vs bio link

Shop tabs and product links are not the same as the Website field. Selling merch in-app is a different setup. The bio link is still the path for coaching, custom work, waitlists, and brand collabs — things Shop does not replace.
FAQ
What does link in bio mean on TikTok? It means the creator put a website on their profile. Watchers leave the video, open the profile, and tap that link.

Do I need 1,000 followers to add a TikTok bio link? Often for a personal account, yes. A business account (and in some places business registration) can unlock Website earlier. Confirm in the app and on TikTok Support.

Why can’t I add a link in my TikTok bio? Usually: personal account under the follower rule, not switched to business, using desktop, or an old app. Website in Edit profile is the clickable field; Bio text is not.
Can I add more than one link on TikTok? Not in the Website field. One URL. Point it at a hub if you need assistant, booking, and collab on one page.
Can I add a TikTok bio link from a computer? Generally no. Use the mobile app.

What is the best link to put in a TikTok bio? The page that matches the video’s ask. For services and DMs, an intelligent bio like PingMyBio. For a single product drop, the product URL. For a pretty list, a link-in-bio tool.
